turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The strongest candidates are those closest to the high-performing selective-contact stacks in the training set:

1. **c030** — The IDTT2FPDI/PCBM/Bphen electron-extraction cascade should provide favorable energetic alignment, strong hole blocking, and reduced interfacial recombination. Its PTAA/PMMA contact closely matches the 19.48% training configuration, with IDTT2FPDI offering additional passivation/selectivity.
2. **c097** — Closely parallels the 18.49% ITCPTC-Th/C60/BCP/P3CT-Na device. The Se-containing acceptor should retain efficient electron transport while improving electronic coupling and interfacial extraction.
3. **c044** — PCBM/BCP with PTAA and Cu is a highly selective, well-supported combination. Related C60/BCP–PTAA–Cu configurations reach 18.62–18.85%; BCP suppresses metal/perovskite recombination and Cu forms a favorable contact to PTAA.
4. **c065** — SFX-PDI4/TiO2 provides a robust electron-selective cascade, while NiMgLiO-c offers high-work-function, electron-blocking hole extraction. The underlying TiO2/NiMgLiO configuration already reaches 18.185% in training.
5. **c088** — C60/BCP–PTAA–Cu is among the best repeated contact combinations in the data. Doctor blading and willow glass may impose a modest film-quality penalty relative to optimized rigid spin-coated devices, keeping it just below the otherwise similar candidates.

**Final: c030, c097, c044, c065, c088**
